chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ghalib ibn Usman, from Rawh ibn Abd al-Rahim, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) urinated, and I was standing by his head, and with me was a container, or he said, a pitcher. So when the flow of urine stopped, he gestured with his hand like this, 'To me.' So I gave it to him with the water, and he performed Wudu in his place.
ai.seo_question: How should one perform Wudu after urinating according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the practical application of Istibra'a, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) waited for the cessation of urine flow before performing Wudu, emphasizing the importance of ensuring purity before ritual washing. The detail of washing 'in the same place' (makānahu) highlights the flexibility in fiqh regarding the location of ablution, provided the area is clean, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ease and practicality in ritual law. It serves as a primary evidence for the method of verifying the end of urination, a critical step often discussed in juristic debates on minor impurity.
